recipes.title: Phở Gà (Chicken Pho)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of pho ga with rice noodles, shredded chicken, herbs, bean sprouts, and lime in clear broth
recipes.prep_alt: Whole star anise, one of the essential toasted spices in an authentic pho broth

sections.heading: Steps
items: Char the onion and ginger over a gas flame or under a broiler until blackened in spots, then rinse off the loose char.
Toast the star anise, cloves, coriander seeds, and cinnamon stick in a dry pot 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken, water, and charred onion and ginger. Bring to a boil, then skim off any foam.
Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, 30-35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, cool slightly, then shred or slice the meat off the bone.
Strain the broth, discarding the solids, and season with fish sauce and rock sugar to taste.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water 10-15 minutes until softened, then blanch briefly and drain.
Divide the noodles into bowls and top with shredded chicken.
Ladle the hot broth over each bowl.
Top with bean sprouts, Thai basil, scallion, cilantro, chili, and a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Bún Chả (Grilled Pork with Vermicelli & Herbs)
recipes.dish_alt: Bun cha Hanoi with grilled pork patties and pork belly floating in nuoc cham, served with vermicelli and herbs
recipes.prep_alt: Julienned carrot and daikon radish, the quick pickle served alongside bun cha

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Nuoc cham (fish sauce, sugar, lime, water, garlic, chili)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Mix the ground pork with half the garlic, shallot, fish sauce, sugar, and pepper, then shape into small flat patties. Toss the sliced pork belly with the rest.
Cover both and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Whisk together the nuoc cham: fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, water, minced garlic, and chili.
Julienne the carrot and daikon and toss with a little vinegar, sugar, and salt; let sit 15 minutes to quick-pickle.
Grill or broil the patties and pork belly slices 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Slide the warm grilled pork into a bowl of the nuoc cham while it's still hot.
Cook the vermicelli noodles according to the package, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Serve the noodles, lettuce, and herbs alongside the bowl of pork in nuoc cham, topped with the pickled carrot and daikon.
Dip noodles and herbs into the sauce bowl bite by bite alongside the pork.

recipes.title: Bánh Mì Thịt Nướng (Grilled Pork Banh Mi)
recipes.dish_alt: A grilled pork banh mi sandwich stuffed with caramelized pork, pickled vegetables, cucumber, and cilantro
recipes.prep_alt: Thin-sliced pork belly ready for the lemongrass marinade before grilling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Combine the pork slices with lemongrass, garlic, shallot, fish sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Marinate at least 30 minutes (overnight in the fridge tastes best).
Heat a grill pan or broiler until very hot. Cook the pork 2-3 minutes per side until charred and caramelized.
Split the baguette lengthwise and toast lightly.
Spread mayonnaise and pâté inside both halves.
Drizzle a few drops of Maggi seasoning over the bread.
Layer the grilled pork inside.
Top with pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, cilantro, and sliced chili.
Press the sandwich closed and slice in half to serve.

recipes.title: Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef)
recipes.dish_alt: Seared cubed beef shaking beef tossed with onion, served over watercress with tomato and cucumber
recipes.prep_alt: Cubed beef seared with onion in a hot pan, the same high-heat technique used for bo luc lac

sections.heading: Steps
items: Marinate the beef cubes with soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, and pepper for 20-30 minutes.
Heat a wok or heavy skillet until very hot with a little oil.
Sear the beef in a single layer, working in batches, 30-45 seconds per side until browned but still pink in the center.
Add the butter and sliced onion, tossing 1-2 minutes until the onion softens and the beef looks glossy.
Arrange the watercress, tomato, and cucumber on a plate.
Pile the beef and onion on top.
Stir the lime juice with a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dipping sauce.
Serve immediately with steamed rice and the lime-salt-pepper dip.

recipes.title: Gỏi Cuốn & Chả Giò (Fresh & Fried Spring Rolls)
recipes.dish_alt: Fresh Vietnamese spring rolls (goi cuon) with shrimp, pork, herbs, and vermicelli visible through the rice paper
recipes.prep_alt: Crispy golden fried Vietnamese spring rolls (cha gio), the other half of this combo dish

sections.heading: Chả Giò Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dried wood ear mushroom, soaked & minced
Rice paper or spring roll wrappers

sections.heading: Steps
items: For the chả giò, mix the ground pork, chopped shrimp, wood ear mushroom, glass noodles, carrot, jicama, garlic, shallot, egg, a splash of fish sauce, and a pinch of pepper into a filling.
Spoon filling onto a wrapper, fold in the sides, and roll tightly into a cigar shape; repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Heat the oil to about 170°C (340°F). Fry the rolls in batches 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Meanwhile for the gỏi cuốn, cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions and drain.
Dip a rice paper wrapper in warm water 10-15 seconds until just pliable.
Lay lettuce, herbs, vermicelli, and pork belly slices near the bottom edge of the wrapper.
Place the shrimp halves cut-side up just above the filling so they show through the wrapper once rolled.
Fold the bottom of the wrapper over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly; repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Serve the fresh rolls with peanut hoisin sauce and the fried rolls with nuoc cham.

recipes.title: Gà Kho Gừng (Ginger Caramelized Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: A pot of Vietnamese ginger caramelized chicken glazed a deep golden-brown in its reduced caramel sauce
recipes.prep_alt: The same pot of chicken mid-braise, absorbing the caramel-ginger sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Marinate the chicken with fish sauce, soy sauce, half the garlic, and pepper for 15-20 minutes.
Make the caramel: melt the sugar in a dry pan over medium heat until deep amber, then carefully add the water off the heat to stop it cooking.
Add the oil, remaining garlic, ginger, and shallots to the caramel and stir until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and stir to coat evenly; sear 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Add a splash of water to just cover the bottom of the pan, cover, and simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked through.
Uncover and let the sauce reduce 3-5 minutes more, until syrupy and clinging to the chicken.
Garnish with scallion and serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Canh Chua (Sweet & Sour Fish Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of canh chua sweet and sour fish soup with pineapple, tomato, okra, and bean sprouts in tamarind broth
recipes.prep_alt: Fresh rice paddy herb, the signature aromatic garnish of an authentic Mekong Delta canh chua

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the tamarind pulp in a little warm water, mash, and strain to make tamarind water (or dissolve tamarind paste directly).
Sauté the garlic in a splash of oil in a pot until fragrant.
Add the tamarind water and remaining water and bring to a boil.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, tasting until the broth is balanced sour-sweet-salty.
Add the fish steaks and simmer gently 6-8 minutes until just cooked through.
Add the pineapple, tomato, and okra; simmer 3-4 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the bean sprouts and rice paddy herb right at the end so they stay crisp and fragrant.
Ladle into bowls and top with fried shallots and sliced chili.

recipes.title: Bánh Flan (Vietnamese Crème Caramel) (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A silky Vietnamese banh flan custard unmolded with dark amber caramel sauce pooling around it
recipes.prep_alt: Eggs, sugar, and milk laid out, the simple three-ingredient base of banh flan custard

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the caramel: melt the sugar with the water in a small pan over medium heat, swirling until it turns a deep amber.
Immediately pour the hot caramel into ramekins, tilting to coat the bottom, and let it harden.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, and vanilla together until just combined, without over-whipping.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve into the caramel-lined ramekins.
Cover with foil, set the ramekins in a baking dish, and pour hot water halfway up their sides.
Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 30-35 minutes, until just set with a slight jiggle in the center.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Run a knife around the edge of each ramekin and invert onto a plate to release the caramel sauce.
